thesis: Round 38 pre-registered cell, on the taxable savings book ($100,000 lump sum, 10-20 year horizon, benchmark 30/70 SPY/AGG, mandate: lowest drawdown of the three books, least return accepted). Base allocation on every card in this field, including the control: 30% SPY (the benchmark's own equity share, so no card here makes an unstated beta bet), 50% AGG, 10% GLD, 10% BIL. Cards differ in exactly one thing -- the tilt condition -- and this round reports treatment MINUS CONTROL, never treatment against the benchmark alone. The programme's prior is a null: rounds 30 and 31 measured every FRED series in the DSL null, and round 32's single inflation near-miss dissolved out of sample. This round predicts a null too (see strategy-program/ROUND-38-PLAN.md section 5); it earns its place by testing a quantity the programme has never formed -- nominal minus breakeven, the real yield -- on a book no macro series has ever been attached to, not by expecting a different answer. It is not a proposal to trade anything, and nothing in a measurement round is promotable. Not investment advice. This is the MANDATORY CONTROL: the same four sleeves and the same 5-point band with every tilt removed, so it carries no rule at all. It is not a treatment that never fires -- it is the static, periodically-rebalanced book every other card in the field is measured as a difference from. Its whole purpose is that a savings card that looks good against the 30/70 benchmark may simply be a better static allocation, which says nothing whatever about the macro condition this round is testing.
falsification: This round's hypothesis is wrong, not merely unlucky, if the treatment-minus-control margin in max drawdown and MAR is indistinguishable from zero across the eligible 5y and 10y rungs -- which is the outcome pre-registered as most likely. It is also wrong in the more interesting direction if the price-only placebo card (r38-price-placebo) moves the same metrics by as much as any macro card does, because that would show the measured effect is 'a tilt fired sometimes' rather than 'the real discount rate carried information'. The named failure regime is a sustained low-real-yield decade with rising equities: from 2013 to 2021 the real yield sat below 1% almost continuously, so a card that de-risks on high real yields spends that entire stretch identical to its own control and can only differ after 2022 -- which means any margin this round reports on the 10-year rungs is dominated by one regime transition, not by nine years of evidence. See ROUND-38-PLAN.md section 6 for the pre-registered per-window firing matrix.
